children: A proposed US sanctions measure targeting Banque Misr's UAE branches is unlikely to directly affect the planned IPO of subsidiary Banque du Caire.
The branches are targeted by a US Treasury Department proposal announced in August that would restrict their access to correspondent banking services with US financial institutions.
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) has received preliminary approval from the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) to acquire Banque Misr’s branch network in the Emirates.

Banking analyst Hany Abou El Fotouh told Zawya the issue is confined to Banque Misr's UAE operations and should not alter the investment case for Banque du Caire, which is majority owned by Banque Misr.

Abou El Fotouh said investors looking at Banque du Caire's IPO will focus on the bank's balance sheet, profitability, growth prospects and future revenue generation, rather than a compliance issue linked to the parent bank's overseas branches.

There is a possibility that the investment bank managing the potential IPO may prefer to wait until the issue is resolved or moves off the headlines before proceeding with the listing, but that remains speculative at this stage, Abou El Fotouh said.
(Writing by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Banque du Caire IPO seen unaffected by US sanctions proposal on Banque Misr's UAE branches
